requested_by: Renee Holloway, IT Audit Manager, Prairie Wind Credit Union
title: Check our sign-in rules and who holds admin rights before the identity audit
situation: Auditors want proof that our sign-in rules work and that nobody keeps admin rights they do not need. We have eight Conditional Access policies (if-then rules that decide what a sign-in needs), a log of 13 recent sign-ins, a list of who holds admin roles, and seven requests from staff to switch on an admin role for a short time. Some rules may be missing, and two people have had full admin rights for years.
your_task: Run each sign-in through every policy and record the outcome: allowed, allowed after MFA (multifactor authentication), stopped for MFA, or blocked.
Note what the report-only (test-mode) policy would have done, without enforcing it.
Flag sensitive apps that no policy protects, and suspicious patterns such as impossible travel.
Review admin role assignments: flag permanent admin rights and check the two emergency (break-glass) accounts.
Approve, hold for approval, or deny each request to switch on an admin role, using the role's rules.
why_it_matters: One stolen password on an account that always has admin rights can hand an attacker the whole company. Sign-in rules that silently miss an app, or old email protocols that skip MFA, are how most account takeovers start.
done_when: Every sign-in has an outcome and the list of policies that applied, with a reason.
Coverage gaps, impossible travel and the report-only results are written up for the auditor.
Each permanent admin assignment has a fix (make it eligible, just-in-time) and the break-glass findings are logged.
Every role activation request has a decision with the rule that drove it.

glossary.Conditional Access: If-then sign-in rules: if this user, app, location, device or risk matches, then block or require extra checks.
glossary.MFA (multifactor authentication): Proving who you are with two or more kinds of proof, such as a password plus a phone prompt.
glossary.Report-only mode: A policy that is tested and logged but not enforced, so you can see its effect before switching it on.
glossary.Legacy authentication: Old email sign-in methods (IMAP, POP, basic SMTP) that cannot ask for MFA.
glossary.Just-in-time (JIT) access: Admin rights switched on only when needed, for a few hours, then removed automatically.
glossary.Standing privilege: Admin rights that are switched on all the time, whether or not they are being used.
glossary.Break-glass account: An emergency admin account kept out of normal sign-in rules so you are never locked out, and watched closely.
glossary.Impossible travel: Two sign-ins for one person from places too far apart to travel between in the time shown.

talking_point: Evaluated 13 sign-ins against 8 Conditional Access policies (4 blocked, 3 allowed after MFA, 2 stopped for MFA), caught an impossible-travel sign-in and an unprotected payroll app, flagged 2 permanent admin assignments and a mis-configured break-glass account, and decided 7 just-in-time admin requests (2 approved, 1 sent for approval, 4 denied).
